more_info.overview: Thaumatin is a preparation of sweet proteins from Thaumatococcus daniellii fruit, with a sweetness far greater than sucrose. It is used to strengthen an existing taste or aroma in the food. The specified material is supplied as cream-coloured powder. The specification identifies water solubility as one of its properties.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain cocoa and Chocolate products as covered by Directive 2000/36/EC; other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.side_effects:
EFSA found no concern for permitted food-use exposure in 2021.
Animal studies supported the absence of relevant adverse effects, with moderate confidence in the evidence.
